purpose: Valproic acid is used to treat seizures, bipolar disorder, and to prevent migraine headaches. It helps calm abnormal electrical activity in the brain that can cause seizures or mood swings. Your doctor may prescribe it alone or along with other medications.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers to communicate between nerve cells. Valproic acid works by increasing the amount of a calming chemical called GABA in your brain, which helps slow down overactive nerve signals. Think of it like a volume control that turns down the electrical 'noise' in your brain that causes seizures or extreme mood episodes.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, or upset stomach especially when you first start taking it. You may also notice drowsiness, dizziness, hair loss, weight gain, or mild hand tremors. Taking it with food can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: This medication can cause serious liver damage, especially in young children and during the first 6 months of treatment. It should NEVER be taken during pregnancy as it can cause serious birth defects and developmental problems in babies. Tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, unusual bleeding, severe stomach pain, or confusion. Regular blood tests are needed to monitor your liver and blood cell counts.
typical_dosing: Doses are very individualized and depend on your condition, weight, and how your body responds. A typical starting dose for adults is 250 mg taken 2 to 3 times a day with food. Your doctor will slowly adjust your dose over time. Always take it exactly as prescribed and never stop suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
